catalog.summary: Start and end date-times with a picker.

valueRules.empty: a request whose both ends are null carries null; the family speaks one word for nothing
valueRules.openEnd: { start, end: null } and { start: null, end } are values: an open end is written in the field, where the reader sees it
valueRules.reversed: an end typed before its start is invalid and stays as typed
valueRules.halves: a PlainDateTime is whole or it is nothing: a date without a time, or a time without a date, lives in the work while the panel is open and in the field's segments, never in the value

pattern.title: Date Picker Dialog Example, for the popup; the tabs pattern for the two ends; the grid pattern for the calendar; the listbox pattern for the list
pattern.rangePattern: none exists; the three patterns the composed families already transcribed, unchanged
pattern.departure: the dialog example closes on the first press and this family closes when the work is whole, because a range with hours is at least four presses; closeOnSelect names the rest

panel.current: one panel, the current end's: the calendar in range mode with both dates drawn, and the list of that end running on that end's day
panel.order: the band with the tabs, the field and the hint, then the presets, then the panel: the calendar and the list of the current end side by side, the list under the grid where the row cannot hold both
panel.labelledBy: the current tab, so a screen reader hears "Pickup, 12 Sep, 14:00" before the first option
panel.day: the list runs on the date of the current end, or on the calendar's focused day while that end has no date; the tab says the date and the hint says "Now the time, 12 Sep" while the time is missing, so panel-day is not needed
panel.why: One end at a time. Two lists side by side, under two fields, were refused at the release gate as too much interface at once for a lay reader and for a phone: two lists of ninety-six rows with 32-pixel targets, a full-screen sheet with no way out, nested scrolling. The tab says which end, the panel shows only that end, and choosing one end moves to the other; the end list appears already striking what the chosen start refuses, in the same gesture.
panel.reversed: the first contract declined tabs with one end at a time because a tablist that exists at one width and not at another tells assistive technology two stories; the tabs now exist at every width, and the DOM does not change with the presentation

list.shape: time-picker's list, unchanged: step, options, maxOptions, unavailableOptions
list.against: the date of its own end, or the calendar's focused day while that end has no date; the day window bounds it, as datetime-picker's list is bounded
list.otherEnd: the other end refuses options only when the two ends are on the same day — the end list refuses the times before the start and outside the duration limits, the start list the symmetric — because on different days the order is the dates', and the grid already imposes it; the duration limits apply across days as well
list.refusedDrawn: a refused option is still drawn with aria-disabled, or hidden with unavailableOptions=hide
list.duration: each option in the list of one end carries, beside its time, the duration the run would have with the other end as it stands — "15:00 · 1 hr" — but only while the two ends are on the same day: across days the rows differ by minutes inside a duration of days, and a column of "3 days 18 hr 15 min" says nothing the band does not; the band's length says the whole, in a live region, in every case

focusRule.rule: the press that leaves the work incomplete carries focus to the half that is missing, swapping the tab when it is the other end's; the press that completes the work closes the panel
focusRule.gridWritesDate: a day pressed for an end that has no time carries focus to the list of that end
focusRule.listWritesTime: a time pressed for an end that has no date carries focus to the grid
focusRule.otherEnd: with its own end whole, the missing half of the other end is next: the tab swaps, and focus goes to its date in the grid, or to its time in the list
focusRule.whole: with the work already whole, a press writes the value and the panel stays open; focus stays where the reader put it

draft.rule: while the panel is open the family holds the work: the two ends as the reader left them, each with its date and time. A press that leaves the work incomplete emits no value; the press that completes it emits the whole run with reason select, and every later press that changes a whole work emits again
draft.halves: each end of the work holds its date and time as two nullable halves, so a chosen day waits for its time and a chosen time waits for its day
draft.abandonedBy: Escape, an outside press and the trigger abandon the work and keep the previous value

length.pending: the duration of the run that would exist if the pending end were chosen — the option under the pointer or the highlighted option of the focused list, or the calendar's pending day — with the other end taken from the work
length.pendingDate: a pending day enters the duration with the time that end already holds, or midnight when it holds none
length.unit: seconds between the two ends, turned into words
length.label: durationLabel(seconds, locale, granularity) by default, replaceable per instance and per provider as lengthLabel(seconds, locale)

highlight.shape: { start: PlainTime | null, end: PlainTime | null }: the highlighted option of each list
highlight.focusedDate: the calendar's own, as in date-range-picker; the family does not hold it

position.meaning: the end whose tab carries aria-selected and data-current, whose field, list and pending band are shown, the end the next press in the grid writes, and where focus goes when the panel opens
position.onOpen: the first end with a half missing; with a whole value, where it was

calendarReceives.end: { start, end: null }, so the next press writes the end instead of restarting the run
calendarReceives.start: the whole value, so the next press restarts the run

position.calendarOrders: when the grid orders the two dates — an end pressed before the start — the hours stay with the end they were on
position.afterGridStart: end, once the start has its time
position.afterGridEnd: the end whose half is missing, or start
position.afterTab: the pressed end, reason pointer or keyboard

now.writes: the current date and time into the current end, both halves, and follows the focus rule
now.why: one now, because one end is shown at a time

step.base: min's time when min is stated, midnight when it is not
step.notTheFieldArrows: the panel's step is the panel's; a segment steps by one of its own unit

opensOn: the cell of the current end
selectionFollowsFocusReason: The listbox pattern lists it as optional and warns it can degrade accessibility. Here a reader arrowing through ninety-six quarter-hours would emit ninety-six requests; the highlight moves, and Enter, Space or a press moves the work.

limits.dayWindow: each list runs between dayWindow(date, { min, max, minTime, maxTime }) for the day of its end — the rule datetime-picker states and MUI declines
limits.crossed: the start field takes max = min(max, end); the end field takes min = max(min, start); the lists take the same, on the same day

contiguous.grid: with an open run, the days beyond the first unavailable day after the start are refused in the grid, through blockedAround as date-range-picker
contiguous.list: on the same day, the options beyond the first unavailable option after the start are refused in the end list
contiguous.search: once per chosen start over the days, up to maxLength days or 366; over the list for the times
contiguous.typed: the day predicate runs over every day between two typed ends and the time predicate over the two ends, once per value change

limits.explained: the limit part names minLength and maxLength while either is set, through the limit.between, limit.atLeast and limit.atMost messages, each duration written by lengthLabel

validity.owned: bounds, the day window, unavailable days and times, the order of the two ends, and the duration
validity.reversed: an end before its start is invalid on the end field and on the frame; the ends are not swapped

clear.fields: the two fields do not draw their own clear; one button on the frame empties both ends with reason clear

preset.value: a DateTimeRange, or a function returning one, resolved on press
preset.invalid: a preset whose range fails a rule still writes it and the value is invalid; the preset is not hidden

wiring.aria-expanded: the trigger, while the popup is showing
wiring.aria-controls: the content, while the popup is showing
wiring.aria-label: the trigger, carrying both ends and the duration

triggerName.chosen: the change message, with both ends in words and the duration in its start, end and length slots; changeReversed, without the duration, while the ends are out of order
triggerName.why: Focus returns to the trigger when the popup closes, so the name is where the reader is told what was chosen.

keyboard.focusTo: the first segment of the current end's field, or its grid where the field is not drawn
the cell of the current end's date, or today when it is empty

keyboard.effect: the other tab, with automatic activation: position moves and the panel swaps
datetime-field's, unchanged, the relative expression included
calendar's, unchanged, including the three views; each move is the pending day and length says the duration

keyboard.key: ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home, End, PageDown, PageUp, a-z0-9
keyboard.effect: time-picker's list keys; each move is the pending end and length says the duration
writes the half; then the focus rule
close, emitting a whole work first

keyboard.staged: the relative expression of the field first; the calendar's view; then the panel closes and the work is abandoned

keyboard.sequence: the tabs (one stop), the field, now, presets, the grid as one stop, the list, footer, done

platformNotes.altArrowDown: ChromeOS turns Alt+ArrowDown into PageDown before the browser sees it, which Angular Material records for its own input. The trigger button is therefore the guaranteed path and the chord is a shortcut, never the only way in.

dismissal.escape: through dismissable-layer, in the capture phase
dismissal.closeOnSelect: auto closes when the work becomes whole, by a press in the grid or a list, by now or by a preset; always closes on any press that changes the value; never closes on none

branches: the trigger, so pressing it again closes rather than dismissing and reopening

responsive.sheet: below 480px on a coarse pointer, the content takes the sheet presentation
responsive.decidedIn: the stylesheet; the DOM does not change
responsive.months: one by default, where date-range-picker draws two: the list sits beside the grid, and two months beside a list do not fit in 720 pixels without wrapping; a consumer who wants two asks for them
responsive.coarsePointer: the rows and the tabs stand at the control height the theme raises to --slotted-target-comfortable; the field is not drawn
responsive.sheetList: four rows and a half under the grid, the only thing that scrolls; the content is capped at 100dvh and scrolls as one when it does not fit, ending with the safe-area inset and done
responsive.presets: a wrapping row of chips between the head and the panel, at every width

portalledIdentity.reason: The family is two subtrees: the control where the consumer wrote it, and the popup portalled to the end of the document. A stylesheet cannot reach a subtree that is no longer inside the root, so data-ui is written on both.

forms.angular: ControlValueAccessor writes the whole DateTimeRange; Validator reports the family's own errors
forms.hiddenInputs: two, on the frame, because the panel in a portal is not inside the form while it is closed

dataAttributes.data-position: on a tab, the field and the panel: start or end
dataAttributes.data-granularity: hour, minute or second, on the root
dataAttributes.data-calendar: the calendar axis, on the root
dataAttributes.data-truncated: on a list: it stops short of the times the configuration asked for, at maxOptions
dataAttributes.data-placement: the side and alignment the positioner resolved
dataAttributes.data-placeholder: on summary and on a tab: there is no value and the text is the placeholder
dataAttributes.data-pending: on length: what is shown is the duration for the pending end, not the work

statePrecedence.guard: every weaker rule carries a :not() for each stronger state it can meet, because specificity rather than source order is what decides between them

literals.--slotted-datetime-range-picker-sheet-in: 100%, which the shared exemption list already holds.
literals.--slotted-datetime-range-picker-list-blo: Eight rows and half of the ninth, counted in the row height the panel states once — the literal time-picker records, for the same reason.

control.shape: one line at the control height: the value written short in the locale, or the placeholder, cut with an ellipsis when it does not fit, a clear, and the trigger that fills the frame
control.why: two datetime fields in one frame need about 360 pixels on one line, a segment cannot shrink, and below that the frame broke into two lines against the control height every form counts on. Withdrawn at the visual gate on the reviewer's reading; a container query could not hide the fields without duplicating them in the panel for typing
control.fullName: the trigger carries both ends in words and the duration, so the ellipsis removes nothing a reader cannot hear

head.holds: three rows: the two tabs; the current end's field and now; the hint, then the length and the limit
head.current: data-current and aria-selected on the current tab, painted whenever the panel is open
head.fieldsSubmit: the field carries no name; the two hidden-input parts on the frame submit startName and endName

tabs.tab: role="tab" on a button, one per end, carrying tab-label and tab-value; aria-selected and data-current on the current end; data-placeholder while the end has no value
tabs.activation: automatic: ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home and End move position with reason keyboard; a press moves it with reason pointer
tabs.value: the end written short in the locale — "12 Sep, 14:00" — a date alone, a time alone, or a dash

hint.says: what the next press should be, or what is wrong: chooseDay while the current end has no date, chooseTime while it has a date and no time; order, length, unavailable or bounds while the work is whole and invalid; empty while the work is whole and valid, when length says the duration
hint.messages: chooseDay with {end} for the end's name; chooseTime with {end} and {day} for the day the list serves; order, length, unavailable, bounds
hint.wiring: aria-describedby of the list and of the field
hint.why: a panel that only refuses — struck rows, a red frame — does not say what can be done; the hint does

done.label: the done message
done.effect: closes with reason pointer; a whole work is emitted with reason select before closing; one end alone stays as it is
done.why: a sheet that fills the screen has no outside to press and no Escape key; on the desktop it is the way out of an edit left half way

field.one: the current end's datetime-field in variant plain, under the tabs, with now beside it
field.finePointerOnly: a segment is a spinbutton, not an input, and raises no keyboard on a phone; the stylesheet does not draw the field under (pointer: coarse)
field.writes: the current end of the work at every request the field emits, with the field's reason; a whole work is emitted as the value
